name: Procurement Strategy
purpose: A project document describing information about specific procurements: how work is delivered, which contract type is used and how the procurement moves through its phases. It is developed once for each procurement when needed.

elements.guidance: How the work is delivered. The blank form prints one Delivery Method box; Table 2.34 splits it into the two rows below.
How the contractor will work with the buyer, for example in a joint venture, as a representative, with or without subcontracting allowed.
The limitations of delivery, such as design-build or design-bid-build.

The contract type, fixed, incentive or award fees, with the criteria for the fees. Common types the book lists: Fixed Price (FFP firm fixed price, FPIF fixed price with incentive fee, FP-EPA fixed price with economic price adjustment), cost reimbursable (CPFF cost plus fixed fee, CPIF cost plus incentive fee, CPAF cost plus award fee) and time and materials (T&M). The blank form prints eight checkboxes (the seven abbreviations and Other) and an Incentive or Award Fee table with a Criteria column.

The procurement phases, milestones, the criteria to advance to the next phase, and the tests or evaluations for each phase, including any knowledge transfer requirements. The blank form prints Phase, Entry Criteria, Key Deliverables or Milestones, Exit Criteria and Knowledge Transfer.

tailoring: A project done with internal resources only needs no procurement strategy.
For a project with few procurements, consider combining this form with the procurement management plan (2.37).

For simple purchases, or a vendor you have worked with successfully for a long time, a formal strategy may be unnecessary; record the information in the statement of work that is part of the contract.
Work with the contracting or legal department so the strategy complies with organisational purchasing policies.

notes: Blank form: PDF page 165 (printed page 154). The blank form prints the abbreviations only for the contract types; the expansions come from Table 2.34. It prints Date, not Date Prepared. The prose's Delivery methods sub-rows (Professional services, Construction services) both map to the single printed Delivery Method box. 'Scope baseline' and 'Project budget' are not single forms and are named, not numbered. Which project documents the fee criteria must agree with is not stated in the book. The alignment 'what_must_agree' texts are reading aids, since the book states only 'aligned and consistent'.
